parsed.refutation_attempt: I investigated whether the call to std::ofstream::open at line 9 could trigger shell command execution. Standard C++ stream opening uses the POSIX open(2) system call with the supplied path as a literal file name; it does not invoke a shell or parse shell metacharacters. I also considered whether special file names (e.g., symlinks, /dev/fd/*) could lead to unintended behavior, but such effects are unrelated to OS command injection and are not covered by the reported vulnerability. No additional checks or sanitisation steps are present that would mitigate a potential command execution scenario. Therefore the claim that an attacker can supply a filename containing shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands is incorrect.
